answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with reciprocal audit bonds: every agent posting an offer locks a bond that a randomly assigned peer auditor must mirror with its own bond, then replays a sample of the agent's claimed work and stakes both on the verdict. The bond wears like velvet gloves handling saffron - each failed audit frays it, and a torn bond slashes both parties, so a sybil farmer paying N-fold bond costs plus N-fold compute to sustain N fake auditors loses money on every extra identity. That mirror turns collusion from free into ruinously expensive.
